item.title: Where to Find Free Warm Clothes During Chicago’s Winter
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaFrom free stores to churches, here are places to get free coats and jackets in the Chicago area.

item.title: Where to Find Warming Centers by Chicago ZIP Code
item.description: Max Herman/Borderless MagazineTemperatures are expected to reach sub-zero levels this weekend and next week. Here’s a list of warming centers across Chicago, organized by ZIP code.

item.title: Despite Fears, Chicago’s Rapid Responders Vow to Continue Facing Down Federal Immigration Officers
item.description: Camilla Forte for Borderless MagazineOrganizers say the work helps their neighbors feel empowered by knowing their rights amid ICE activity. They say more community members have joined since Trump took office.

item.title: Borderless Magazine Selected for LION Growth Grant
item.description: Borderless Magazine has been selected as one of 15 publishers nationwide to receive a $100,000 grant from LION Publishers. The two-year operational grant will support Borderless Magazine in strengthening its business operations and long-term sustainability.

item.title: TPS Protections Are Expiring. Here’s What To Know About the Latest Changes to the Immigration Program
item.description: Photo illustration by Max Herman/Borderless MagazineWith Trump attempting to terminate TPS for countries like Myanmar/Burma and the protections expiring for others, over a million immigrants are in legal limbo.

item.title: What to Know When Filming ICE
item.description: Dave Decker/ZUMA Press Wire/AlamyAs immigration enforcement escalates following multiple fatal ICE shootings, Borderless Magazine spoke with an attorney on what to know when exercising your First Amendment right.

item.title: New SNAP Eligibility Changes Could Leave Thousands of Immigrants, Refugees Without Food Assistance
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaOfficials are working to connect individuals with food assistance as over 340,000 Illinois residents — including 14,000 legally present immigrants with humanitarian protections — could lose SNAP benefits amid new eligibility changes.

item.title: SNAP 2026: What To Know About New Federal Changes
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaNew work eligibility rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, known as SNAP, is set to start Feb. 1. Borderless Magazine breaks down who's still eligible, what to know about these changes and what immigrants can do now.

item.title: Mayor Puts ‘ICE On Notice,’ Calling On Chicago Police To Investigate Crimes By Federal Agents
item.description: Colin Boyle/Block Club ChicagoThe ‘ICE On Notice’ executive order provides a framework for police and the Mayor’s Office to document and investigate alleged wrongdoing by immigration officers so they can be held criminally accountable, Mayor Brandon Johnson’s office said.

item.title: Between Two Countries: Inside A Venezuelan Woman’s Journey To Find Safety
item.description: Illustration by Jen Chavez for Borderless MagazineFearing deportation in Chicago, a Venezuelan national returned to her home country, but Maduro’s capture made her once again uncertain about her future and safety.
